constraints: ZDR must propagate: any /learn or Save-as-skill that distils a conversation is a content-persisting boundary and must reuse the sessionreview rule (refuse unless the run explicitly declares zdr:false). Promotion to org scope stays an owner/admin decision. Skills are scoped org or user by a CHECK constraint, so Space libraries need a schema change, and Space access must not widen an owner-plane ACL. Today the background loop enables machine-written skills immediately, so a proposal path (F-t3-007) conflicts unless the loop is changed too. Schema ownership is split: agent_skills migrations live in session-core while capability-core also writes the table.
approachAdjustment: Choose a single owner and table before versioning: live skills are agent_skills rows updated in place, while skill_packages is an unused scaffold in capability-core; add immutable version rows with a digest (reuse ContentHash), record skill id plus version on the turn, and re-key the quarantine by version so a rewritten skill does not inherit old demerits. Ship the thin layer first (authoring doctrine, a linter on every upsert path, /learn and Save-as-skill through the proposal path) because it needs no schema change, then versions, then libraries and import. Make the background loop propose rather than enable if proposals are the intended path.
effortNote: Raised from L: as written it spans skills, frontend slash templates and agent presets, Space libraries with a schema change, import, and curation. Doctrine, linter, /learn and Save-as-skill alone are S to M; versions alone are L.
verdictReason: Skill CRUD, sharing, provenance protection, a learning loop, content hashing and quarantine already exist, while versions, libraries, import, authored presets, /learn and a linter are absent. Reword to the missing parts and split into a thin first layer and a versioning layer.

constraints: ZDR: the ledger envelope carries the zdr flag and the gateway publisher suppresses zdr envelopes (per a capability-core retention.go comment), so a live meter on ZDR turns must be computed in-stream from provider responses, not read back from cost-core. Quotas and billing policy are owned by Control Plane (org_quotas), so the ceiling comes from there and the warning is advisory; a mid-run stop is out of I16 scope because budget.rs is a pre-flight check only. Subscription routes have no list price, so the meter shows tokens or quota percent there. Estimates must be labelled, never promises. New events go through the ChatEvent family gate so old clients ignore them.
approachAdjustment: Start from plan I16 (progress frames plus warning) and add the cache read/write fields to the existing Usage frame, since the data already flows from inference-core to the ledger. Surface the silent 80 percent tier downgrade to the user as part of the warning instead of building a second threshold. Drop "extend the usage record with reasoning tokens" (providers report reasoning as a subset of output, not a disjoint count) and treat role, tool and subagent attribution, thread aggregation and the plan-card estimate as separate later work. Per-user allowance needs Control Plane billing support because only org-level allowances exist today.
effortNote: Unchanged as a whole; the core (progress frames, live meter, 80 percent warning, cache fields) is M per plan I16, while pre-run estimate, attribution and per-user allowance are the L remainder.
verdictReason: Much of the supporting data and surfaces already exist (cost basis, ledger cache tokens, org allowances, quotas with reset, subscription windows) and the live meter is already planned as I16; reword to the genuinely missing parts and split the core from the estimate and attribution work.
